variants.text_note: No mark at all. ต is a mid-class consonant, so an unmarked live syllable is mid tone.
Mark ้ (mai tho). Saying this about food claims you are making it up.
Mark ๋ (mai chattawa). Note tone 4 is skipped: with a mid-class initial, ๊ would be high and there is no everyday word for it here.
No mark. Final ง keeps the syllable live.
Mark ่ goes after the consonant cluster and BEFORE the vowel อ.
Mark ้. In a market this is the pair that bites: ask for the camera and receive a cardboard box.
No mark. The everyday verbal sense; เกาะ 'island' is a different word and not part of this set.
Mark ่. Saying this about goods in a market reads as an insult and wins you a discount you did not ask for.
Mark ้. Ask for the price of item nine and you have instead called it old.

NO MARK, and this is tone 5 — not tone 1. ข is a HIGH-class consonant, so an unmarked live syllable is rising. Every textbook says 'no mark = mid', and that is true only of mid-class initials. This is the single most common mislabelling in Thai learning material and this set exists partly to disprove it.
Mark ่. Low here regardless of class, so this one is safe.
Mark ้, which is FALLING for this initial and not high. Ask for rice and get white — the stall has white signs, white bowls and white rice.
No mark. ค is a LOW-class consonant, so the unmarked slot is mid — same as mid class, different reason.

Mark ่, which is FALLING for a low-class initial and NOT low. Many learners are taught that mai ek is always low; it is not. This is the set that breaks that habit. Renderer note: ำ is a single codepoint U+0E33 and the mark goes BEFORE it.

variants.text_english: to prop up, support; a guarantor
variants.text_note: Mark ้, which is HIGH for a low-class initial — not falling. The only tone-4 member in the tone stage, and the only one reachable because low-class initials map ้ to 4.
